original_text: ### REQ-X-007: Charity verification and sanctions **Source questions:** OD-02, TVC-006, TVC-007, TVC-040, TVA-009, TVA-028, TVR-SAN-001-Q, TVR-SAN-002-Q, TVF-027, TVF-048. **Normative proposed requirement:** Unbound maintains one authoritative, standardized charity-vetting framework and reusable evidence/status across sponsors. original_text: SOC2-024: Control owners MUST periodically attest to operation, and independent reviewers MUST challenge evidence completeness and effectiveness.
statement: Each control in the register MUST be classified MachineEvaluated or Manual. A Manual control (e.g. board approvals, related-party review, vendor due diligence, policy approval) MUST be attested by its owner at its stated frequency. An independent reviewer MUST, at least quarterly, review coverage metrics (MON-009), open deficiencies and a reviewer-selected sample of Manual-control attestations, and MUST NOT be the owner of any control in that sample.
reason_for_change: Periodic owner attestation of machine-evaluated controls repeats information the evaluation already records; at ~90 master-matrix controls it is ~360 h/yr [D] of signatures that detect nothing the monitor does not. Independence is kept by reviewing coverage, deficiencies and manual controls.

original_text: ### REQ-X-007: Charity verification and sanctions **Source questions:** OD-02, TVC-006, TVC-007, TVC-040, TVA-009, TVA-028, TVR-SAN-001-Q, TVR-SAN-002-Q, TVF-027, TVF-048. **Normative proposed requirement:** Unbound maintains one authoritative, standardized charity-vetting framework and reusable evidence/status across sponsors. A vetted charity does not undergo duplicate routine vetting solely because another sponsor uses it. Record scope, evidence provenance, effective date and expiry; reverify at least every 180 days, on material changes, and check current sanctions/eligibility at execution. Adverse findings propagate to all affected sponsors. Sponsor-specific grant restrictions and approvals remain distinct from common charity vetting; no self-approved vetting exceptions. Cross-sponsor legal reliance, liability, jurisdictions and recipient classes require counsel validation; model never clears holds. **Acceptance scenario (not executed):** Given a recipient verified 30 days ago and sanctioned today, when payment releases, then the current adverse signal holds the grant despite valid periodic review. **Open dependencies:** Formal owner validation, evidence, test implementation and source migration.

statement: A comprehensive charity revalidation whose evidence satisfies the published FreshnessPolicy (UNB-RCN-GRT-014) and the sponsor's versioned eligibility rules with no contradictory, stale-critical or adverse signal MUST renew assurance with no human action. A grant whose recipient has current assurance, a passing per-sponsor reliance snapshot at approval and at release (RR-REQ-X-007-r1), no hold, and which falls within a board-delegated routine policy (OD-01) MUST proceed without human vetting review. Human review MUST be created only with a reason code from {MissingEvidence, ContradictoryEvidence, AdverseSignal, IdentityAmbiguity, NonStandardClass (ED/ER/SO/fiscal sponsor/non-filer), PolicyAmbiguity, SourceUnavailableBeyondPolicy} after bounded automated evidence gathering, and each item MUST carry its HumanInterventionClass (UNB-SMP-ORG-001). Fully passing renewals and grants MUST be included in the independent stratified sample (UNB-XIN-CLM-005) without blocking. When a completed grant is later found to have gone to an ineligible recipient or for a prohibited purpose, the platform MUST open an ExciseTaxIncident (UNB-XIN-NPG-008), invalidate the affected assurance for all sponsors relying on the shared factual claim, hold unfulfilled grants to that recipient, and record recovery actions; it MUST NOT reverse fund accounting except through the governed correction path.

rationale: Eliminates routine human vetting touches while keeping accountability and correction paths explicit.

original_text: ### REQ-X-007: Charity verification and sanctions **Source questions:** OD-02, TVC-006, TVC-007, TVC-040, TVA-009, TVA-028, TVR-SAN-001-Q, TVR-SAN-002-Q, TVF-027, TVF-048. **Normative proposed requirement:** Unbound maintains one authoritative, standardized charity-vetting framework and reusable evidence/status across sponsors. A vetted charity does not undergo duplicate routine vetting solely because another sponsor uses it. Record scope, evidence provenance, effective date and expiry; reverify at least every 180 days, on material changes, and check current sanctions/eligibility at execution. Adverse findings propagate to all affected sponsors. Sponsor-specific grant restrictions and approvals remain distinct from common charity vetting; no self-approved vetting exceptions. Cross-sponsor legal reliance, liability, jurisdictions and recipient classes require counsel validation; model never clears holds. **Acceptance scenario (not executed):** Given a recipient verified 30 days ago and sanctioned today, when payment releases, then the current adverse signal holds the grant despite valid periodic review. **Open dependencies:** Formal owner validation, evidence, test implementation and source migration.
statement: In addition to RR-REQ-X-007-r1: (1) A scheduled deep review that finds all required evidence current and passing under the active policy version SHALL renew the common verification automatically, recording the policy version as the approving authority, with no human sign-off where the sponsor's delegated policy permits (OD-01). (2) Renewal SHALL start no later than the FreshnessPolicy refresh lead time, with load-spreading, so that an expired deep review holds new approvals only when renewal has failed. (3) Event-triggered revalidation (RR-UNB-EXT-028-r1) SHALL reset the deep-review clock only when it performs a full review. (4) A verification reused by a second sponsor SHALL NOT trigger new routine vetting; that sponsor's policy overlay and per-grant reliance snapshot SHALL still be evaluated. (5) Automatically renewed verifications SHALL be independently reviewed after the fact, without blocking grants, under the common risk-based sampling policy of UNB-XIN-CLM-005 (as revised 2026-11-24): each stratum declares a confidence level and tolerable error rate from which the sample size follows. A fixed sample of 30 MAY be used only as an exploratory pilot and SHALL NOT be reported as assurance (zero errors in 30 still leaves an upper 95% error bound near 10%). (6) The platform SHALL report renewal success rate, evidence reuse ratio (grants per verification), time-to-detect material adverse events, false-hold and false-clear rates.
reason_for_change: Product-owner review 2026-11-24 (QR-0007): Replace universal 30 with risk/error-bound sampling; 30 is exploratory only (zero errors in 30 still allows roughly 10% upper 95% error bound).

statement: The system SHALL monitor source updates, status changes, leadership changes, financial-filing changes, enforcement events and entity relationships for every charity with an open grant, active schedule, unreleased payment or grant in the prior 24 months. Each detected change SHALL be classified by a versioned, counsel-approved MaterialityTable into: (a) Material-Adverse (e.g. revocation, sanctions listing, dissolution, bankruptcy, EIN change, successor designation, supporting-organization type change, change matching a sponsor DiscretionaryGrantPolicy criterion) -> publish a hold to the hold registry within the policy's detection SLA, re-evaluate only impacted grants and schedules (UNB-GEX-019), apply UNB-XIN-NPG-005 effects, and open one case per charity and reason; (b) Material-Neutral (name change same EIN, address change) -> apply deterministic effects without a case; (c) Informational (leadership change, routine filing) -> update evidence with no hold, no case and no human task. Each monitored source MUST declare its freshness: its publication lag and, per decision (approval, release), the maximum age of evidence accepted. Decisions MUST use cached verified evidence within the approved window and MUST NOT require a live provider call for every payment; when evidence is older than the window or the source is unavailable, the decision MUST fail safe (hold, never pass). No acknowledged financial fact (class C0) may be lost by a recovery unless an approved recovery procedure states the loss semantics, the compensating records and the customer notice.

statement: Before a platform-maintained policy-pack version is published, the system MUST shadow-evaluate it against each adopting sponsor's decisions of at least the prior 90 days using pinned evidence, and MUST produce a per-sponsor diff of changed outcomes. Publication MUST require sign-off by the pack owner when any sponsor's changed-outcome share exceeds a declared threshold. Activation MUST be staged: the version becomes effective for at most one sponsor (or one declared cohort) first and for others only after the first stage has processed a declared representative volume covering each risk stratum the change affects, no reassessment trigger has fired, and rollback of that version has been rehearsed; elapsed time alone (for example seven days) MUST NOT satisfy the observation criterion. Each pack parameter MUST declare either an ordering (so "tighten only" is checkable) or an enumerated set of approved alternatives. Rollback to the prior version MUST be a single versioned action.
reason_for_change: Product-owner review 2026-11-24 (QR-0035): Seven days is illustrative; require representative volume, risk coverage and rollback readiness, not elapsed time alone.

original_text: **UNB-GOV-002:** Every policy parameter that changes approval, eligibility, agent permissions, financial limits or risk SHALL be versioned, reviewed, tested and independently approved.
statement: Every policy parameter that changes approval, eligibility, agent permissions, financial limits or risk MUST be versioned and automatically back-tested against the historical corpus before publication. A material change to financial controls, eligibility, agent permissions, financial limits or customer rights MUST require independent approval, with author different from approver, whether it loosens or tightens. Single-approver handling is allowed only for changes classified low-risk under an independently approved change policy; mixed or ambiguous changes are material. Classification of a change as tightening MUST be computed, not self-declared. Back-testing MUST use representative history plus synthetic edge cases.
reason_for_change: Product-owner review 2026-11-24 (QR-0027): Reject the blanket one-approver tightening exception. Independent approval for material changes to financial controls, eligibility, permissions or customer rights regardless of direction; streamlined low-risk changes only within an independently approved change policy; ambiguous or mixed changes are material. The estimated 50 hours/year saving is unvalidated.
business_objective: Policy agility with independence where risk increases.
processing_rules: Version and back-test all changes.
Compute loosen/tighten.
